title: Fix a running toilet
safety: Turn off water supply valve first.
steps: Shut off supply.
Drain tank.
Inspect/replace flapper.
Adjust fill valve.
Test flush.

title: Fix a leaking faucet
safety: Shut off water first.
steps: Shut off water.
Relieve pressure.
Remove handle.
Replace cartridge.
Test.

title: Windows won’t connect to Wi-Fi
steps: Restart router + PC.
Forget + rejoin network.
Update driver.
Run troubleshooter.

title: OBD-II P0300 misfire — what to check
safety: Do not drive with flashing check-engine light.
steps: Read freeze-frame.
Check plugs/coils.
Check vacuum leaks.
Seek mechanic if unresolved.

title: Replace lawn mower spark plug
safety: Disconnect plug wire, cool engine.
steps: Remove wire.
Remove plug.
Gap new plug.
Install + reconnect.

title: Unjam a garbage disposal
safety: Turn the disposal switch OFF and unplug it (or flip the breaker). Never put your hand inside.
steps: Cut power at the switch and breaker.
Find the hex socket on the disposal bottom and work an allen wrench back and forth to free the jam.
Use tongs (never fingers) to pull out the lodged object.
Press the red reset button on the disposal bottom.
Restore power and run cold water while testing.

title: Fix a sticking interior door
safety: None — hand tools only.
steps: Mark the rub spots with pencil while opening/closing.
Tighten all hinge screws; long screws in the top hinge fix most sag.
Sand or plane only the marked spots, a little at a time.
Seal bare wood so humidity doesn't swell it again.

title: Patch a small drywall hole
safety: Check for wires/pipes behind the wall before cutting.
steps: Trim loose edges and stick the mesh patch over the hole.
Spread joint compound thin with a putty knife, feathering edges.
Let dry, sand smooth, apply a second thin coat if needed.
Prime and paint to match.

title: Re-caulk a bathtub
safety: Ventilate the bathroom; silicone fumes irritate eyes.
steps: Cut out all old caulk and clean with rubbing alcohol.
Tape both sides of the joint for a clean line.
Apply a steady bead of silicone, then smooth with a wet finger.
Pull tape immediately; let cure 24 hours before showering.

title: Replace a standard wall outlet
safety: Turn OFF the breaker and VERIFY dead with a voltage tester before touching anything. If wiring looks aluminum or scorched, stop and call an electrician.
steps: Kill the breaker; test the outlet dead with the voltage tester.
Remove cover and outlet; note which wires go where (photo helps).
Connect black to brass, white to silver, ground to green.
Mount, restore power, and test with a lamp or tester.

title: Stop a chirping smoke detector
safety: Never disable a detector — replace batteries or the unit.
steps: Press the hush/test button to identify the chirping unit.
Replace the battery (or batteries) with fresh lithium.
If it still chirps, the unit is expired — replace it (10-year life).
Test monthly going forward.

title: Jump-start a dead battery
safety: No smoking near the battery; keep cables clear of moving parts. If the battery is cracked or leaking, don't jump it — replace it.
steps: Park the donor car close; both engines OFF.
Red clamp to dead battery positive (+), red to donor positive.
Black to donor negative (-), black to unpainted metal on the dead car.
Start donor, wait 2 minutes, start the dead car.
Remove cables in reverse order; drive 20+ minutes to recharge.

title: Fix a TPMS low-pressure warning
safety: Check pressure cold; don't drive on a visibly flat tire.
steps: Find the correct PSI on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Check each tire cold with a gauge.
Inflate to spec (including the spare if it has a sensor).
Drive a few miles — the light should reset; if not, a sensor may be bad.

title: Diagnose squealing brakes
safety: Use jack stands — never work under a car on a jack alone. If braking feels weak or the pedal sinks, tow it to a shop.
steps: With the wheel off, check pad thickness (under 3mm = replace).
Look for a wear indicator tab touching the rotor.
Clean dust with brake cleaner; check the rotor for deep grooves.
Replace pads as an axle set if worn; bed them per the box instructions.

title: What to do when the engine overheats
safety: NEVER open a hot radiator cap — scalding steam. Pull over and shut off immediately if steam appears.
steps: Pull over safely and shut the engine off; turn the heater to max while coasting.
Wait at least 30 minutes for it to cool.
Check the coolant reservoir (not the radiator cap) and top up if low.
Look for leaks/hoses; if it overheats again quickly, tow it — don't drive.

title: Replace a headlight bulb
safety: Don't touch a halogen bulb's glass with bare fingers — oil shortens its life.
steps: Open the hood and find the bulb socket behind the headlight.
Unplug the connector and twist the socket out.
Wearing gloves, insert the new bulb without touching the glass.
Reconnect, test, and aim-check against a wall at night.

title: Free up a full iPhone
safety: Back up photos before deleting anything.
steps: Settings > General > iPhone Storage — see what's biggest.
Offload unused apps (keeps data) and delete what you don't need.
Enable iCloud Photos 'Optimize Storage' or move videos to a computer.
Clear Safari cache: Settings > Safari > Clear History and Data.

title: Fix a printer stuck offline
safety: None.
steps: Restart the printer and your router.
On the computer, remove the printer and re-add it.
Make sure the printer and computer are on the same Wi-Fi network.
Reinstall the manufacturer's driver if it still shows offline.

title: Fix slow Wi-Fi
safety: None.
steps: Unplug the modem and router for 60 seconds, then plug the modem back first.
Move the router central and elevated, away from microwaves.
Switch congested devices to 5GHz in your Wi-Fi settings.
If speeds stay low at the modem, call your ISP.

title: Speed up a slow Windows PC
safety: Don't disable security software at startup.
steps: Task Manager > Startup apps — disable what you don't need at boot.
Settings > Storage — run Disk Cleanup / Storage Sense.
Check for Windows updates and install them.
Uninstall programs you no longer use.

title: Fix a mower that won't start
safety: Disconnect the spark plug wire before working; no smoking near fuel.
steps: Check fuel — drain old gas (over 30 days) and refill fresh.
Check oil level; top up with the right weight.
Pull and inspect the spark plug — clean or replace if fouled.
Reconnect, prime per the manual, and pull firmly.

title: Replace a broken sprinkler head
safety: Turn the zone off at the controller first.
steps: Turn the irrigation zone OFF.
Dig around the head and unscrew it from the riser.
Screw on the matching new head to the same height.
Turn the zone on and adjust the spray pattern.

title: Get rid of aphids on roses
safety: Spray in the evening to protect pollinators; follow label directions.
steps: Blast colonies off with a strong hose spray.
Spray insecticidal soap directly on remaining aphids.
Repeat in 5–7 days; encourage ladybugs as natural predators.
Avoid broad insecticides that kill beneficial insects.

title: Diagnose an oven that won't heat
safety: Turn OFF the breaker before removing any panels. Gas oven? If you smell gas, leave and call the gas company.
steps: (Electric) Kill the breaker; inspect the bake element for blisters or breaks.
Unplug the range, remove the element's mounting screws, and swap in the matching part.
Restore power and test at 350°F.
If the new element doesn't heat, the thermostat or control board is suspect — call a pro.

title: Fix an ice maker that stopped
safety: Unplug before removing panels.
steps: Confirm the ice maker arm/switch is ON and the freezer is at 0°F.
Check the water supply valve behind the fridge is open.
Replace the water filter if it's past due — clogs starve the maker.
Wait 24 hours; if still nothing, the inlet valve may need a pro.

title: Stop a sparking microwave
safety: Stop using it immediately when arcing. Never run a microwave empty.
steps: Unplug and inspect for metal (foil, twist ties, chipped-rack coating).
Clean food splatter off the walls and waveguide cover.
Replace a burned waveguide cover with a microwave-safe one.
If arcing continues with nothing inside, the magnetron is failing — replace the unit.

title: Remove a stripped screw
safety: Wear eye protection when drilling.
steps: Try a larger bit or a wide rubber band between bit and screw.
Tap the driver firmly into the head while turning.
Use a screw extractor: drill a pilot hole, then back the screw out.
Replace with a new screw — don't reuse the stripped one.

title: Hang a heavy picture level and secure
materials: wall anchors rated for the weight
safety: Use anchors rated above the frame's weight; find studs for heavy pieces.
steps: Weigh the frame; choose anchors rated above it.
Mark hanger spots with a tape measure and level line.
Drill, set anchors, and mount the hangers.
Hang, level, and give it a firm tug test.
